source.repro: node --experimental-transform-types plugins/wiggle/benches/densitySubpixelFloor.ts --file=test_data/volvox/volvox-sorted.bam.coverage.bw --refName=ctgA --start=20000 --bpPerPx=3.25 — it prints both scenes and all six arms. No GPU: the quads are flat and opaque, so the GPU arms apply the one rule every rasteriser implements for them, a sample taking the colour of the LAST quad covering it, over the shader's own extendToMinWidthPx. The Canvas2D arms are drawDensity itself, on node-canvas.
source.notes: Ground truth is MAF_SUBPIXEL_CELLS' own: the unfloored geometry supersampled (16x here) and box-downsampled, which is the bp-weighted mix a pixel should hold. The supersampled arm has to be the UNFLOORED one, because a CSS-px floor does not shrink away at high dpr the way MAF's device-px floor did. `ink` is that doc's `chroma` under the name it has here: the density ramp runs white to the track colour, so max(r,g,b)-min(r,g,b) reads how much colour the row carries, which is what a floor inflates. Scene: volvox-sorted.bam.coverage.bw at ctgA:20000, 1000 CSS px at 3.25 bp/px — the raw section, 1-bp records, 0.308 px a bin, deliberately off the 4x sample grid that an integer bp/px lands on. The sparse scene keeps every 8th of those records, 0.308 px marks with 2.3 px of white between them. The shipped GPU path is 4x MSAA: deriveSampleCount gives 4 unless every pass declares `coverage: analytic`, and wiggle's fill and density passes do not.
